clue.text: Worries about a mass of ice

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the synonym for the first word is read from the back

parts.note: worries as a noun means cares

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a glacier or an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns CARES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A serac is a pinnacle or ridge of glacial ice, so it is a mass of ice.

clue.text: African inhabitants bring charges against Europeans immigrating

indicators.note: immigrating means coming into a country, so the second piece moves inside the first

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against
Danes are people from Denmark

explanation.surface: Africans take legal action against incoming Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'immigrating' is the container signal: the Europeans come into the word for legal action, as immigrants enter a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese are the people who live in Sudan, an African country.

clue.text: Glance, oddly erotic, taking in church

indicators.note: taking in means holding something inside, so one piece goes within another
oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strangely racy look is exchanged in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges the six letters into RICOET, and 'taking in' sets church's abbreviation inside them. 'Glance' looks like a look but is the bounce-off sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To ricochet is to glance off a surface and rebound, as a bullet does.

clue.text: Regain consciousness, well after we blow, on reflection

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Regain consciousness, well after we blow, on reflection': COME TO is regain consciousness and on reflection defines it, but 'well after we blow' gives nothing for THINK OF IT; the OCR clue is likely garbled and the scan is blank
annotationWithheld.clue: Regain consciousness, well after we blow, on reflection

clue.text: Note returned ever and again, interrupted by another

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole run built from the following words is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something interrupted by another thing has it breaking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music and theatre to call for something again
another note after the first: ME, a spelling of mi in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A musician repeats a note over and over until another cuts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole run backwards, BIMES being BIS split open by 'interrupted by'. 'another' is a second note following the 'Note' at the start; BIS is the encore call.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a whole note in music, the longest note value in common use.

clue.text: One who is bound to search the net the sound of it

indicators.note: the sound of it means the word is pronounced, not spelt, giving a word that is said the same

parts.note: to surf is to browse the internet

explanation.surface: A captive spends their time browsing the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to work his lord's land.

clue.text: Doctor put an -e-mail out

indicators.note: out means not in its proper order, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician has sent out an email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUTANEMAIL; 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is a verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to falsify or tamper with it, which is to manipulate it.

clue.text: Support for seamen working on this Arabian scow

indicators.note: working on suggests the letters are processed and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors are busy aboard a flat-bottomed Arab boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working on' rearranges the fifteen letters of 'this Arabian scow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain's chair is a seat slung from ropes that supports a sailor working aloft or over the side.

clue.text: Mate set up, with king finally falling into snare

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the word is read from bottom to top
finally falling means the last part drops away

parts.note: a mate is a partner
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player sets a trap where the king finally falls to mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally falling' drops the last R (king) from PARTNER, and 'set up' turns PARTNE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch in a snare or trick someone into a trap.

clue.text: Avoid points to argue over

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
to chew over is to debate or discuss

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps matters to be debated.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to deliberately avoid or abstain from something.

clue.text: A hundred tales of French romance concocted

parts.note: the French word for 'of' is de

indicators.note: something concocted is made up or mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes up a hundred French love stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges the seven letters of 'romance' into CAMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a medieval collection of one hundred stories told over ten days.

clue.text: In part I convey

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the following words is used, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: Someone says they only partly get their meaning across.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the letters of 'part' itself: p-ART-I-C-onvey; the whole clue is also the definition, since an articulated lorry conveys goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An artic is an articulated lorry, a British term for a large truck that carries freight.

clue.text: Resort to extremely tiny and subtle distinction

parts.note: Nice is a holiday resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the outermost letters of the next word are kept

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker heads to a tiny resort and makes a fine point.
explanation.walkthrough: TY is the first and last letters of 'tiny'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or precise distinction, often a subtle one.

clue.text: Turncoat has a delivery of mail, a note

parts.note: the post is a delivery of letters
te is the seventh note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A traitor receives the morning post along with a short message.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who abandons their faith or party, a turncoat or renegade.

clue.text: Strive to capture ram -—- scold and curse

indicators.note: to capture is to hold within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to vie is to strive or compete
tup is a dialect word for a ram
to rate is an old word for scold

explanation.surface: A farmer struggling to catch a ram scolds and swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to capture' is the container signal: the striving word holds the animal, and the old sense of scold follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To vituperate is to curse or berate someone with abusive language.

clue.text: Bill presented after dessert — that's a bloomer

parts.note: sweet is a British word for a dessert or pudding
Bill is a short form of the name William

explanation.surface: A bill is handed over after the pudding course, which is a big mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented after' puts the name following the pudding. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is a garden flower, and a bloomer here is anything that blooms.

clue.text: South American girl finds accommodation in the outskirts of Brighton

indicators.note: finding accommodation in a place means staying inside it
the outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman finds lodgings on the edge of Brighton, a seaside town in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' takes B and N from Brighton, and 'finds accommodation in' puts OLIVIA between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivian describes a person from Bolivia, a country in South America.

clue.text: Alienate English oddball

parts.note: as an adjective oddball means odd or strange

explanation.surface: An eccentric Englishman drives people away.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate someone, making them unfriendly or distant.

clue.text: On time's usual, but it's different to be absolutely together

indicators.note: it being different means the words before are changed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, including the s of time's, are the fodder

explanation.surface: Being punctual as normal is something different from doing things all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Things simultaneous happen at exactly the same moment, completely together in time.

clue.text: Start season well

definitions.meaning: to start is to leap up suddenly, to jump
a well is a natural source of water

explanation.surface: Begin the season well.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring means to jump up, the season after winter, and a natural source of water.

clue.text: Group of trees in a ring? On the contrary, a rut

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, here reversed by what follows
on the contrary turns the containment round, so the trees go round the ring instead

parts.note: a grove is a small group of trees
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Trees growing in a circle turn out to form a furrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the trees go inside the ring; 'On the contrary' swaps it, putting O inside GROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel, and to be in a groove is to be in a rut.

clue.text: Parrot puts a scratch into dog, perhaps

indicators.note: into means the following pieces are placed inside another word

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet, shown by perhaps
to rake is to scratch or scrape

explanation.surface: A parrot claws at the family dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'dog, perhaps' gives a category the dog belongs to, a household animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed kind of parrot.

clue.text: Feeling more pain, hide greeting in tree

indicators.note: to hide something is to tuck it away inside something else
in places the greeting within the tree's name

parts.note: acer is the maple genus of trees
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Someone in pain conceals a hello inside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' and 'in' together signal the container; the tree is the maple genus, a common crossword tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Achier is the comparative of achy, so it means suffering more aches.

clue.text: Noise from farmyard goes over river upland

parts.note: a moo is the sound of a cow

explanation.surface: A cow's lowing carries across the river to the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'goes over' puts MOO on top of R.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is an area of open, uncultivated high ground, an upland.

clue.text: One number, played very loudly, is foul

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A single number blasted out at top volume turns out to be offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: An in-off is when the cue ball goes into a pocket after hitting another ball, a foul in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker and billiards an in-off is a foul stroke that pots the cue ball.

clue.text: Bill's speech expressing love

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, abbreviated ad
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A man named Bill gives an address declaring his love.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and devotion, a synonym for love as a noun.

clue.text: Plough rather big to carry

parts.note: great means very big, a step up from big
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A farm plough is too large to lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' looks like farm equipment but is the star pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plough is the British name for the group of seven bright stars in the constellation Ursa Major, the Great Bear.

clue.text: Colour starts to run in narrow streaks earthwards

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Paint dribbles downwards in thin lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a temporary hair dye, used to colour the hair.
